summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin, chronic abdominal pain, and anemia was admitted for lower abdominal pain and dark stools. She had not had a bowel movement in five days, and imaging showed diverticulosis without acute diverticulitis. Her hemoglobin was 6.5 g/dL, and she received two units of packed red blood cells for acute on chronic anemia. She was found to have hyponatremia and hypokalemia. A urine culture grew enterococcus, and she was discharged on a five-day course of amoxicillin. Pulmonary edema was treated with diuresis, and repeat imaging showed improvement, though she required home oxygen due to persistent desaturations with activity. Warfarin was held during admission due to melena and not restarted at discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for anemia, anticoagulation, and infection resolution.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
